newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil health minister quits over money squabbles.
newsitem.headline: Brazil health minister quits over money squabbles.

text.p: Brazilian Health Minister Adib Jatene resigned on Tuesday following frequent disagreements with the government's economic team over funding health services, officials said.
Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso had made a last appeal to persuade Jatene to remain, but the minister remained firm in his decision to quit.
"The funding issue was the main motive for his dissatisfaction," Amaral said, referring to Jatene.
Jatene, a leading Brazilian cardiologist, had been expected for weeks to resign over what newspapers reported was anger at tight-fisted Finance Ministry officials.
The minister scored a victory against his own government in September when he won congressional approval for a new temporary tax to fund the health services.
But the Finance Ministry balked at advancing money to the Health Ministry before the new 0.2 percent tax, to be levied on financial transactions, comes into effect in January.
Amaral said Executive Health Secretary Jose Carlos Seixas will take over temporarily as the new health minister.
